output.takeaways:
Revenue Growth:
NVIDIA’s revenue growth has shifted from negligible levels in 2023 (0.2%) to explosive expansion in 2024 (125.9%) and 2025 (114.2%). This inflection is directly tied to surging global demand for accelerated computing and AI-driven data center infrastructure, segments where NVIDIA’s compute and networking products are dominant. The ability to more than double revenue in consecutive years highlights not just expanding end-markets, but also NVIDIA’s increasingly vital position in the AI ecosystem. Such growth is rare at this scale, reflecting a powerful first-mover advantage and deep integration in large cloud and enterprise deployments, enhancing its competitive moat and bargaining power.

Gross Profit Margin:
NVIDIA’s contribution margin jumped from 56.9% in 2023 to 72.7% in 2024, stabilizing above 70% thereafter. This significant margin expansion points to effective pricing power and a favorable product mix tilted toward high-value GPUs and enterprise AI solutions. Elevated gross margins demonstrate both technical leadership and limited competitive encroachment, suggesting robust differentiation and continued customer willingness to pay a premium. These factors combine to reinforce the view of NVIDIA as a quality business with sustainable competitive advantages.

SG&A Expense Margin:
SG&A as a percentage of revenue has declined rapidly, dropping from 9% in 2023 to just 2.1% in 2026 and projected to fall even further. This reflects tremendous operating leverage as the business scales, with revenue growing much faster than operating costs. Such a trend illustrates management’s disciplined execution and NVIDIA’s inherent scalability, driven by the capital-efficient nature of its fabless business model and high-margin software-accelerated growth. For investors, this underscores confidence in margin protection even as topline grows rapidly.

EBITDA Margin Stability:
NVIDIA’s EBITDA margin rebounded from a cyclical trough of 22.2% in 2023 to over 66% in 2025 and 2026, dramatically outpacing competitors (e.g., AMD’s 2025E EBITDA margin is far below, with less than $8bn EBITDA versus NVIDIA’s $86bn). While NVIDIA’s EV/EBITDA was historically elevated (81x in 2023), it compresses (to 33.8x in 2025), improving the investment case as EBITDA surges. The peer-leading margin profile signals superior profitability and capital efficiency, justifying a premium multiple. This margin leadership positions NVIDIA as the quality outlier in the semiconductor universe, supporting a strong investment thesis anchored on durable earnings power, cash flow generation, and differentiated market positioning.
